newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil drifts, not so tight as the Med.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil drifts, not so tight as the Med.

text.p: High and low sulphur fuel oil was broadly unchanged on Thursday with little support gained from the Portuguese tender for up to five cargoes, traders said.
The market was looking more balanced than the fundamentally tight Mediterranean.
The high sulphur barge market divided between a lacklustre prompt sector where prices were talked at $112-113 fob ARA for prompt material and up to $114 fob ARA for October barrels.
For end-October deliveries the bull run appears to have eased since prices were talked down to $111-112 fob ARA.
Views varied as to whether the barge market was able to absorb the Russian straight-run cargoes (up to four) which were heard headed into the sector.
High sulphur cargoes were seen a touch softer around $106-107 fob NWE, off $1 or so in line with today's sparse enquiry levels.

Low sulphur cracked fuel was slow again on Thursday amid rising speculation as to when the main Med buyer will begin its stockbuilding ahead of the winter. Some traders feel the buyer will not be as active a buyer this year which could act as a bearish long term cap to firmer prices.
